input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct ROCm validation campaign for vLLM serving

## Description

Run a functional and performance parity validation campaign for vLLM serving
of the platform's supported model set on physical AMD Instinct accelerators,
producing the per-model go/no-go data that determines the scope of ROCm
serving runtime productization. This epic resolves the strategy's central
unknown — whether upstream vLLM ROCm builds reach functional and performance
parity with the productized CUDA builds for the models RHOAI supports — which
no readable artifact can answer; the answer must be produced by executing the
campaign on hardware.

## Scope

- Define the validation test matrix covering every model in the supported
  model set for vLLM serving, including the serving configurations and AMD
  Instinct hardware topology used for each run.
- Execute functional validation per model: serving behavior and output
  correctness compared against the CUDA baseline on the same model set.
- Execute performance validation per model: throughput and latency parity
  data versus the CUDA baseline.
- Record per-model results with hardware, driver, and ROCm image versions
  used for each run.
- Produce a final report stating a go/no-go recommendation per model and the
  resulting productization scope (the set of models that clear).
- Securing AMD Instinct hardware access (procurement or partner lab) is part
  of this epic's work; the access path is unresolved (see Risks and Notes).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation plan and test matrix exists that covers every model in the
  supported model set, recording the serving configurations and hardware
  topology used.
- Functional results are recorded per model as pass/fail against the CUDA
  baseline for the same model set.
- Performance parity data (throughput and latency) is recorded per model
  against the CUDA baseline.
- A final report states a go/no-go recommendation per model and the resulting
  productization scope.
- All recorded results originate from executions on physical AMD Instinct
  hardware, with the hardware, driver, and ROCm image versions documented.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks and Notes

- **Hardware access (availability precondition, externally controlled):**
  dedicated AMD Instinct nodes do not exist in the CI fleet, and procurement
  vs. partner-lab access is unresolved. This gates campaign start and cannot
  be compressed by engineering effort; it is a risk, not an acceptance
  criterion — the epic's deliverable (the validated report) is what the ACs
  measure. Partner-lab terms may additionally constrain which models can be
  run and whether performance numbers are publication-grade.
- **Upstream ROCm image cadence:** the campaign consumes upstream ROCm builds
  of vLLM, whose release timing is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; available versions may constrain the test matrix.
- **Size (one logical change above the ~2-week guideline):** estimated at
  roughly 3–4 weeks of calendar effort once hardware access is secured
  (functional plus performance validation for every model in the supported
  model set on externally-gated physical hardware). Kept as a single epic
  because it is one mechanical campaign — one test matrix, one environment
  bring-up, one per-model go/no-go report consumed as a unit by downstream
  productization and documentation. Re-split trigger: if execution exceeds
  one sprint (2 weeks) of run time after hardware access is secured, or the
  model set grows beyond what one sprint can cover, split per model or into
  functional vs. performance phases (functional first — it alone can shrink
  the performance matrix).

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

Productize a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by
the AMD Instinct validation campaign: build and release the ROCm runtime
image variant, package it as a platform serving runtime, and validate KServe
compatibility on AMD GPU nodes. The runtime's supported scope is definitionally
the set of models the validation campaign clears; if fewer models clear than
the full supported set, this epic productizes the cleared subset.

## Scope

- Build and release a vLLM ROCm runtime image variant from the midstream vLLM
  repo, pinned to a recorded ROCm base image version from upstream releases.
- Configure the Konflux build pipeline for the ROCm image variant in the
  already-onboarded Serving Runtimes build machinery (no separate onboarding
  needed — the component is Konflux-onboarded).
- Define and ship the ServingRuntime (or ClusterServingRuntime) for the ROCm
  vLLM runtime, requesting amd.com/gpu resources and targeting AMD Instinct
  nodes.
- Validate KServe compatibility (KServe itself requires no code changes —
  accelerator support is runtime-level): InferenceServices using the ROCm
  serving runtime deploy and reach Ready on AMD GPU nodes.
- Record the supported (cleared) model set in the runtime's support
  metadata.
- Ensure coexistence with existing CUDA-based serving runtimes — the ROCm
  runtime is additive; existing runtimes are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm runtime image build exists in the midstream repo, pinned to a
  recorded ROCm base image version.
- The Konflux build pipeline for the ROCm image variant is green.
- A ServingRuntime CR deploys the ROCm vLLM runtime with amd.com/gpu
  resource requests for the cleared model set.
- KServe InferenceServices using the ROCm serving runtime reach Ready on AMD
  GPU nodes.
- Existing CUDA-based serving runtimes deploy and serve unchanged (no
  regression; the new runtime is additive).
- The supported (cleared) model set is recorded in the runtime's support
  metadata.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.
- Supports HLR-4 inputs: the recorded supported model set feeds the
  documentation.

## Risks and Notes

- **Upstream ROCm image cadence (externally controlled):** whether AMD's
  runtime image releases align with our release trains is outside our
  control; a pinning/mirroring strategy for the ROCm base image may be
  needed to keep the productized runtime aligned with release trains.
- Scope is gated by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome: if no models
  clear, productization is cancelled and the campaign report feeds a
  follow-up strategy decision.

# PyTorch ROCm training support in the Training Operator

## Description

Enable PyTorch training on ROCm through the Training Operator: single-GPU and
multi-GPU (distributed) PyTorchJobs scheduling and running on AMD Instinct
nodes using PyTorch ROCm worker images, with admission through Kueue covered
by the platform's queueing stack.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob worker pods to schedule and run on AMD GPU nodes with
  amd.com/gpu resource requests (node placement on AMD Instinct nodes).
- Support single-GPU and multi-GPU (distributed) PyTorchJob topologies on
  ROCm.
- Use and document verified/pinned PyTorch ROCm worker image references for
  supported training jobs.
- Validate training execution on AMD Instinct hardware: jobs run to
  completion and distributed initialization works across workers for
  multi-GPU topologies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu resources runs to completion
  on AMD Instinct nodes.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu resources runs to completion
  on AMD Instinct nodes with distributed initialization across workers.
- Verified/pinned PyTorch ROCm worker image references are documented for
  supported training jobs.
- Existing NVIDIA GPU PyTorchJob execution is unaffected (no regression; AMD
  support is additive).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling
  (quota/admission side covered by the Distributed Workloads epic).

## Risks and Notes

- **Physical hardware dependency:** validation requires physical AMD Instinct
  nodes, the same hardware whose access path (procurement vs. partner lab) is
  unresolved for the serving validation campaign. This is a shared
  resource-coordination risk, not a structural dependency on the serving
  campaign's outcome — training enablement proceeds independently.
- PyTorch ROCm worker images are published upstream; no upstream
  contribution is required, but available image versions follow the upstream
  release cadence.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm training workloads

## Description

Enable and validate quota handling for amd.com/gpu resources in the
Distributed Workloads stack so that PyTorch training jobs on ROCm are admitted
through Kueue with correct quota accounting and all-or-nothing (gang)
semantics for multi-GPU jobs.

## Scope

- Quota configuration for amd.com/gpu resources in the Kueue quota model
  (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue) covering AMD GPU node flavors.
- Admission of single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs requesting amd.com/gpu
  through Kueue, with all-or-nothing admission for multi-GPU job topologies.
- Validate quota accounting: admitted workloads' amd.com/gpu usage counts
  against configured quota, and workloads queue when quota is exhausted.
- Verify no regression to existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling and admission.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota configuration supports amd.com/gpu resources
  for AMD GPU node flavors.
- A single-GPU PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted through Kueue
  against the configured quota.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted with
  all-or-nothing semantics under the amd.com/gpu quota.
- Quota accounting for amd.com/gpu is correct: usage of admitted workloads is
  reflected in quota consumption, and workloads queue when quota is
  exhausted.
- Existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling and admission behave unchanged.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling
  (job execution side covered by the Training Operator epic).

## Risks and Notes

- **Physical hardware dependency:** end-to-end admission validation requires
  AMD GPU nodes and a runnable ROCm training workload; this shares the
  unresolved AMD hardware access path with the serving validation campaign
  (resource-coordination risk, not a structural dependency).
- Coordinating a shared end-to-end validation run (a multi-GPU ROCm
  PyTorchJob admitted under amd.com/gpu quota) with the Training Operator
  work is a planning concern; each side's acceptance criteria can be verified
  independently.

# AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement documentation

## Description

Document AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for RHOAI: supported AMD hardware, driver
prerequisites, and the validated model list for serving, plus PyTorch ROCm
training support and amd.com/gpu quota configuration. Authored after the
implementation work so the docs describe what was actually built and
validated.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Supported AMD hardware: the AMD Instinct accelerators supported for serving
  and training.
- Driver and software prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes (ROCm driver
  requirements and node preparation).
- The validated model list for vLLM ROCm serving, as cleared by the AMD
  Instinct validation campaign and reflected in the productized runtime's
  supported scope.
- PyTorch training on ROCm: supported job shapes (single- and multi-GPU),
  PyTorch ROCm worker image usage, and Kueue quota configuration for
  amd.com/gpu.
- Explicit out-of-scope statements matching the strategy: no Intel Gaudi or
  other non-AMD accelerator families; no AMD GPU sharing/partitioning
  support.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation topics state the supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list.
- Training documentation covers single- and multi-GPU PyTorch ROCm job shapes
  and amd.com/gpu quota configuration through Kueue.
- Out-of-scope statements (non-AMD accelerators, GPU sharing/partitioning)
  are documented.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented outcomes
  (validation campaign report, productized runtime scope, and training
  enablement results).
- Content accuracy is validated against the platform architecture context
  and the validation campaign results.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list. (Epic priority is P1 per the
  docs-authoring priority exception — strategy priority Major → P1 — rather
  than inherited from HLR-4's P2.)

## Risks and Notes

- The validated model list is not known until the AMD Instinct validation
  campaign reports; documentation authoring is sequenced after the campaign
  and the implementation epics for this reason.
